newsitem.title: CHINA: China central debt depository plans big expansion.
newsitem.headline: China central debt depository plans big expansion.

text.p: China's newly launched national state debt depository plans to boost the number of members to 500 in the year 2000 from the current 30, the China Securities said on Monday.

The central depository, the China Government Securities Depository Trust and Clearing Co, began operations in June as part of official efforts to boost debt trading on a unified market that limited risk from repurchase trading.

Beijing has ordered a shift of debt trading from stock exchanges and local state debt trading centres to the depository which is now responsible for clearing all debt trading and trust holding operations.

At present, the depository has over 30 members including more than 20 commercial banks, the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges, a number of large-sized trust firms and stock brokerages, the newspaper said.
It would allow more financial institutions to become trust and clearing members in 1998, the newspaper quoted a report by the depository outlining its plan for future development.
The company aims to have more than 500 members in the year 2000, with some members acting as market-makers, dealers and clearing banks, it said.
The depository expects China to open its state debt market to foreign investors once its currency -- the yuan -- becomes fully convertible, the newspaper said.
"Once the yuan become an international currency, China's state debt market will open its door to the outside world without the least hesitation," it said.
China's central bank officials have the yuan probably would not be made convertible on the capital account until the early years of the next century.
China made the yuan convertible on the current account last year.
